reasons: The rule expects an insurance covenant and none exists: the cited General Provisions run to 18.14 with no insurance obligation, and Article XVI contains only indemnity/recall language, so 'missing' is the correct classification rather than fallback.

The rule is genuinely applicable here — Array manufactures and supplies Product, sponsors Clinical Studies and gives product-liability/recall indemnities to Ono under 16.2 — so uninsured indemnity exposure is a real credit risk for our side.

The redline is actionable and minimal: it appends a single new Section 18.15 after 18.14 without disturbing existing text, imposes the obligation one-sidedly on Array (no reciprocal burden on us), and tracks the preferred limits (CGL 1M/2M, E&O 2M, cyber 5M, workers' comp, certificates on request) with sensible pharma-specific adaptation (products/clinical trial liability; cyber conditioned on Array handling our data).

Drafting hooks are consistent with the agreement (defined 'Term', 'Clinical Studies', 'Law', 'Confidential Information'), and the deterministic checks confirm the insurance obligation is present in the inserted text.

The comment is accurate, concise, in first person plural, explains what changed and why, cites the playbook position and offers the E&O 1M / cyber 2M fallback without lecturing; the caveat about the separate Supply/Quality Agreement possibly carrying manufacturing cover is noted in the rationale rather than overstated.
